memory_update.text: TENB should be carried forward as the most direct underfollowed public-market mapping for OT cybersecurity tied to AI data-center and critical-infrastructure exposure; key survival test is whether OT Security revenue/materiality can be verified.

ITRI is an adjacent automation candidate, not a pure cybersecurity name. It belongs in the node only if grid-edge software, DERMS, managed services or utility operations workflows show recurring revenue and switching-cost evidence.

The critical-infrastructure cybersecurity chokepoint appears to split into three subnodes: OT exposure/asset management, utility/grid automation workflows, and privileged/machine identity for hybrid cloud and regulated infrastructure.

Several strong OT secure-remote-access vendors found in search, including Xona, Dispel, Netop, TDi Technologies and OPSWAT, appear private or not cleanly US-listed; later layers should map public acquirers, distributors or embedded partners.

node: Cybersecurity and automation software embedded in critical infrastructure operations
summary: Layer 1B expands this node with one high-attention reference anchor and three underfollowed small/mid-cap candidates. The strongest underfollowed fit is Tenable because its filings explicitly identify Tenable OT Security and frame OT/ICS/SCADA risk as expanding with AI data-center buildouts. Itron is a less obvious utility-operations automation candidate rather than a pure cybersecurity vendor; its grid-edge intelligence, DERMS, distributed intelligence and utility endpoint footprint make it relevant to critical infrastructure workflow embedding. Belden is a hybrid hardware/software OT networking and cybersecurity candidate with mission-critical industrial-network exposure, less obvious because it screens as connectivity/infrastructure rather than software. Palo Alto Networks is included only as a reference anchor after completing the CyberArk acquisition, which validates identity/PAM as a strategic control point for AI-era infrastructure security.
